title: The Four Flags
premise: Decoration Day on the old camp-ground is the one day in the year nobody in the valleys shoots anybody. Pritchard has used it to put four flags on four poles and four speakers at one table: the Compact, the Commonwealth, the Dominion and the Directorate, each with an offer for a valley that has just learned somebody is paying to keep it poor. There is dinner on the ground, a fiddle contest and a beef shoot. There is a courteous stranger in a grey duster who wins the shoot without trying. Then a courier comes in off the high country with a tin case chained to her wrist, and the truce lasts as long as it takes a bullet to cross a fairground.

places.name: The camp-ground
places.what: A meadow outside Mercy Crossing with an old meeting shed, a burying ground dressed with paper flowers, plank tables, four flagpoles and a long table under them

places.name: The shooting line
places.what: A rope on the grass, a steer tied to a post, charred boards at sixty paces, Ada Pike with a pair of dividers

places.name: The meeting shed roof
places.what: Where the shot came from: a bell-rail, wet shingles, and one empty silver case standing on end

stages.set_by: Walking onto the camp-ground on Decoration Day, after Three Roads to Ruin completes
stages.log: Four flags, one table, dinner on the ground. Pritchard says nobody has drawn a gun on Decoration Day in forty years and he would take it kindly if you were not the first.

stages.set_by: Paying a share of the steer at the shooting line
stages.log: You are in the beef shoot. Ada Pike judges. The shot to beat belongs to a woman with a string of silver cases round her neck.

stages.set_by: Putting the closest shot to the cross
stages.log: Ada Pike laid her dividers on the board and said your name. You own the hind quarter of a steer.

stages.set_by: Being beaten at the shooting line
stages.log: Edda Flint drove her nail. You did not. She did not gloat, which was worse.

stages.set_by: Speaking with the man in the grey duster
stages.log: A stranger in a grey duster split the cross at sixty paces with a pistol and gave the beef away. He looked at you a moment too long.

stages.set_by: The courier reaching the long table, or the last shot of the beef shoot, whichever is first
stages.log: A courier came across the meadow at a dead run with a tin case on her wrist. She was three steps from Pritchard when the shot came off the meeting shed roof.
You went after the shooter: over the tables, up the shed, across the roof and down to the river.
You stayed with her. She said: lights on Blackstone ridge. Trains on the dead line. Then a number, twice, and nothing else.

stages.set_by: The button '(Stand between the rifles and the crowd)'
stages.log: Brigg's line had their rifles up and four hundred people in front of them. You walked into the middle and stood there. Nobody fired.

stages.set_by: The button '(Take the case and go)'
stages.log: You cut the case off her wrist and went out through the burying ground while everybody was looking at the roof.

stages.set_by: Reaching the bell-rail on the meeting shed roof
stages.log: One empty case, silver, standing on end on the bell-rail where it would be found. Edda Flint was already there. She put it on her string.

stages.set_by: Opening the tin case, alone or on Pritchard's desk
stages.log: The courier's case holds a strip of brass punched with holes, a sketch of a ridge with lamps drawn on it, and one line of writing: a ledger number, in Silas Vane's hand.

stages.set_by: Brigg's order, an hour after the shot, unless stage 43 is set
stages.log: The Dominion holds the camp-ground. Brigg says it is for the public safety and will be for as long as the public is unsafe.

stages.set_by: Pritchard reading the line in the case, or the player reading it if the case was taken
stages.log: Pritchard read the number twice and sat down. He has eaten supper with Silas Vane for twenty years.

objectives.text: Hear what the four flags are offering
The courier is down. Do one thing, now

options.label: (Go after the shooter)
options.now: A chase over the roof to the river. He gets to the skiff. He tips his hat
options.later: You have seen his face and his gun. Flint decides you are worth talking to. The crowd is left to Brigg

options.label: (Stay with the courier)
options.now: You hear her last words and keep the case out of other hands
options.later: You alone know the number she carried in her head as well as on paper. The shooter is a rumour

options.label: (Stand between the rifles and the crowd)
options.now: Brigg's men lower their rifles. He does not take the camp-ground
options.later: The valley remembers who stood there. So does Brigg. The case may be in anybody's hands by nightfall

options.label: (Take the case and go)
options.now: You have the case and nobody knows it
options.later: Every flag wants what you carry. You can sell it, read it or burn it. Pritchard learns who took it

evidence.found: Standing on the bell-rail of the meeting shed roof
Ada Pike, shown the silver case: it came from a mould with a maker's mark filed off, and she knows whose

ways_through: Walk onto the camp-ground, be there when the shot comes, and open the case with Pritchard afterward. Needs no match shot, no chase and nothing optional.
Chase the shooter to the river and come back for the case.
Stay with the courier and carry what she said to Pritchard.
Take the case and read it alone; the chapter completes on reading the line.
cannot_break: The shooter cannot be caught or killed here: the skiff is always a boat-length out. If the player is not on the camp-ground when the courier arrives, the shot is heard from wherever the player is and stage 70 follows. If Pritchard is somehow absent the case is opened by Talbot, or by Keene if Talbot is in her clinic. If the player shoots first on Decoration Day the Dominion takes the camp-ground at once and the courier is shot in the confusion all the same. Nobody at the table can be killed in this chapter.

open_questions: May the silver gun's owner walk onto the stage in Act I, unnamed, and speak to the player? Everything he says can be cut and the shot still comes off the roof.
He and the surveyor both look at the player as though they know them. Nothing is said. Is even that too much before the choices about the player's past are settled?
The four flags are named people from the registry. Are Whitcomb and Brigg wanted here in person, or their juniors?
How does the Directorate show itself in a valley that does not know what it is? Here it is a surveyor who offers to bring the power back.
The courier is the first Hollowborn the player sees. Nobody remarks on it. Is that the right way to meet one?
